and the outlet, and what was read for it. With no `edition`, the reader's own (made ea

tools.name: top
tools.description:
The stories of the last 24 hours in rank order, run again hourly (`as_of`, `window_hours`): each story's
rank, our title, its score (0-1: the edition's perspective, its mains pulled by the edition's stakes), `mains`
(the main at the edition's home and at the world, the honest pair), its outlets, our

tools.name: why
tools.description:
Why a piece's story is where it is on the list: its rank and score, the mains at the edition's home and at
the world, its scores each under its title, the stakes that lifted it, what cut a main (no outlet abroad told
it, a routine notice), who carried it, who it is about, what is just above and belo

tools.name: story
tools.description:
One story over time: its name, where it stands (Now, Peak and Run, 0-1, each with its `basis` and
`known_from`; rising, steady, fading or quiet; whether it moved since `since`), its days in order, each with
its size and its top happening's title, our page and the outlet's link, and its strands. Free

tools.name: ongoing
tools.description:
The biggest running stories at the edition's home (or a country), biggest Now first, one row a story: where
it stands, its numbers and its latest day's top happening with our page and the outlet's link. Free. Ask one
by its `story` for its days.

tools.name: search
tools.description:
The stories of the last `days` whose pieces name the query, one row a story, in our words with its lead
piece's outlet and link, our story page, how many pieces it was found in, its outlets and days, its score and
its place on today's list: today's list first, then by score, then the newest. Costs o

tools.name: save_interest
tools.description:
Move one of the reader's magnets, what draws their own edition: a `target` and a step (away, low, normal,
high) saves at once. For a subject no target names, a `draft` of their own words: without `preview` it answers
what the draft would give a day, the pieces it finds, and a `confirm` digest; with

tools.name: my_interests
tools.description:
Every magnet that draws the reader's edition, theirs over the edition's, with the words they gave, and
their credits.

tools.name: set_brief
answer_brief
tools.description: The question set_brief asked, answered: the choice put in the record, which is compiled again.

tools.name: rehearse_brief
tools.description:
The mornings of the last days the brief would have given, lane by lane: each line a happening with our
title and page and the main it was ranked by; a quiet lane says so. From the pool alone; nothing is saved.

tools.name: save_brief
tools.description:
The brief kept, on the reader's yes: their active record, its lanes drawing their own edition from the next
morning. Refused when the record changed since its `confirm`.

tools.name: my_brief
tools.description:
The brief the reader holds, with its plain-language read-back and the `confirm` an amendment saves on; or what
stands in its place.

tools.name: amend_brief
tools.description:
The whole brief as amended by one sentence of the reader's, compiled as set_brief does, with `changes`
against the one they hold. save_brief with the new `confirm` keeps it.

tools.name: forget_brief
tools.description:
The reader's brief dropped, only when they asked for that in words: nothing draws their morning but the
world's. Their history stays on the site.

tools.name: delivery
tools.description:
Start or stop the reader's edition by mail each morning, or their private podcast feed, only when they ask.
Mail goes to the address they signed in with; the podcast answers a feed link for their podcast app, theirs
alone. The same call again changes nothing.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "why" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
